note: xs-on + reply-off golden captured from dev BEFORE any reply implementation (fabric reply-plan §8.4). Never regenerate to fix a diff.

list_sessions.name: list_sessions
list_sessions.label: list_sessions
list_sessions.description: List other explicitly-joined main sessions on this machine's web hub (fabric cross-session). Each row carries a short ref, optional name, cwd, receive policy and busy state. Address them with message_session using the ref.

query.description: Optional filter over session refs and names (prefix or exact-name match).

scope.description: "hub" (default): every joined session on this hub. "cwd": only sessions in the same directory tree — filters this listing only, never limits sends.

message_session.name: message_session
message_session.label: message_session
message_session.description: Send a message to another joined main session on this machine's web hub (fabric cross-session; the recipient sees it as untrusted input). Reply to an incoming cross-session message by messaging its from.ref. effect "applied" = delivery confirmed; "none" = provably NOT delivered (safe to retry later); "unknown" = the message may have entered the recipient's queue — it usually becomes visible at the recipient's next turn boundary; do NOT blindly resend.

to.description: Target session: a short ref from list_sessions, a full session id, or a session name. Reserved forms (root, system, main, r_…, @…, wf_…) are rejected — those address runs and labels, not sessions.

text.description: Message body. Truncated to fabric.maxChars (75% head + 25% tail) before sending.

wake.description: Omit or false (default): deliver only. true: also wake the recipient session — EXPENSIVE, it starts a model turn there; rate-limited and chain-depth-limited, and past any limit it is downgraded to deliver-only with the reason in wakeDowngraded.
